steps.title: Gamay
steps.body: Almost all Beaujolais is Gamay, fully Gamay Noir à Jus Blanc. It gives light to medium-bodied reds with red cherry, raspberry, violet and fresh acidity, and low tannin. Beaujolais has nearly all the world's Gamay. Pruned in gobelet, bush style, on the hills, it suits granite's poor, well-drained soils.

steps.title: Carbonic maceration
steps.body: Much Beaujolais uses semi-carbonic maceration. Whole bunches go into a tank; the bottom ones are crushed and ferment, releasing carbon dioxide. The upper berries ferment inside their skins, giving fruity aromas like banana, bubblegum and cherry, with little tannin. Some crus use more traditional methods for structure.

steps.prompt: What does semi-carbonic maceration give Beaujolais?
steps.explanation: Whole-berry fermentation gives fruity, soft wines.

steps.title: Beaujolais Blanc
steps.body: A small amount of Beaujolais Blanc is made from Chardonnay, mostly in the north, near the Mâconnais. It's fresh and fruity, similar to Mâcon. Rosé is also made from Gamay. But red Gamay is over 95% of production.

steps.prompt: Which are features of Gamay in Beaujolais?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Semi-carbonic maceration gives fruity, soft wines
A little Chardonnay makes Beaujolais Blanc
